claim: Analyzing dependency graphs to redesign execution. (a) Critical-path analysis identifies the longest weighted dependency chain, which sets a latency floor of 12 seconds in this illustrative graph. Two possible responses are shown. (b) Decomposing the dominant operation into independent suboperations reduces the modeled critical path to 7 seconds, excluding coordination overhead. (c) Changing the information dependencies can remove a serial constraint altogether. In DocAble’s image-description pipeline, replacing propagation of previously generated descriptions with shared rendered context allowed the image-description operations to proceed independently.
topology: The upper weighted graph branches at A and joins at F. The lower left splits B into three parallel children. The lower right compares a chain between image descriptions with two independent consumers of the same page context.
bw_encoding: Gray fill marks the expensive or modified work. White boxes denote other operations. Arrowheads show prerequisite order.
redesign: Follow the weighted critical path, then compare two distinct redesigns: split an expensive operation or remove an unnecessary information dependency.
alt: A weighted graph branches after A. The path through B and D takes 12 seconds, while the path through C and E takes 6 seconds. Three concurrent 3-second parts of B shorten the critical path to 7 seconds before overhead. In DocAble, two image-description operations become independent when each receives its image and shared rendered page context.
